simple.meaning: מִכְסָה (mikçâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an enumeration ; by implication, a valuation.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 12:4. The surrounding context includes priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִכְסָה (H4373) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

structuredEvidence.definition: an enumeration ; by implication, a valuation

firstOccurrence.englishText: and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls. You shall make your count for the lamb according to what everyone can eat.

timeline.evidenceText: and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls. You shall make your count for the lamb according to what everyone can eat.
then the priest shall reckon to him the worth of your valuation up to the Year of Jubilee; and he shall give your valuation on that day, as a holy thing to Yahweh.
